sources.locator: HTML Living Standard; living standard accessed 2026-07; provisions applicable to Linked resources and loading hints
sources.claim: Stylesheets, scripts, icons, and preload hints declare external resources with loading behavior that can affect rendering, execution order, security, and performance.

canonicalExplanation.summary: Pages pull in other files: stylesheets with `<link rel="stylesheet">`, scripts with `<script>`, icons, fonts. How they load matters. A normal stylesheet **blocks rendering** until it arrives (so the page doesn't flash unstyled). A plain `<script>` in the head **blocks parsing**; `defer` and `type="module"` scripts download in parallel and run after parsing. Hints like `preload` fetch something early — use them sparingly, only for truly critical resources.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
Your page shows a blank white screen for two seconds. DevTools shows a 400 KB analytics script in the head, loaded before any HTML was parsed. Meanwhile, a teammate added `preload` to twelve files and made things slower. A noncritical module script loads with module semantics while the main stylesheet remains a normal render dependency. In this lesson you'll configure document resources and explain their loading relationship.

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.body: You should know the **Document foundations**, **Text and page semantics** and **Forms and native controls** modules, plus **Relative and absolute URLs** and the **Standards-mode document skeleton**.

sections.heading: The model: what blocks, what waits
sections.body:
```html
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <title>Course home – Codestead</title>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/main.css">          <!-- render dependency -->
  <link rel="icon" href="/favicon.svg" type="image/svg+xml">
  <script type="module" src="/js/quiz.js"></script>     <!-- deferred by default -->
  <script src="/js/analytics.js" defer></script>         <!-- runs after parsing -->
</head>
```

| Resource | Loading behaviour |
|---|---|
| stylesheet link. | blocks rendering until loaded. |
| classic script. | blocks parsing. |
| `defer` script. | downloads in parallel, runs in order after parsing. |
| `type="module"`. | deferred by default; supports import. |
| `async` script. | runs as soon as it arrives, order not guaranteed. |
| `preload`. | fetch early — only for critical late-discovered files. |

```reveal
{"prompt": "Why not preload every file?", "answer": "Preloads compete for bandwidth. Preloading non-critical files delays the critical ones, making the page slower."}
```

sections.heading: Measure it

includes: Link stylesheets, icons and scripts with correct loading attributes.
Explain render-blocking, parser-blocking, defer, module and preload behaviour.

outcomes: Configure document resources and explain their loading relationship.

examples.title: Main stylesheet and a module script
examples.situation: A noncritical module script loads with module semantics while the main stylesheet remains a normal render dependency.
walkthrough: **Main stylesheet:** `<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/main.css">` remains a normal render dependency, so the page never flashes unstyled.
**Noncritical module script:** `<script type="module" src="/js/quiz.js">` loads with module semantics — downloaded in parallel and run after parsing.
**Measure:** the Performance panel will show HTML parsing finishing before quiz.js runs.
examples.result: The page renders styled content quickly, and the quiz script runs without blocking the parser.

examples.title: The preload pile-up
examples.situation: A developer adds `<link rel="preload">` for 12 images, 4 fonts and 3 scripts. Largest Contentful Paint gets slower.
walkthrough: All 19 files compete for bandwidth at the start.
The hero image the user actually needs first arrives later.
Fix: remove preloads except for one critical late-discovered resource (e.g. the hero font), then re-measure.
examples.result: With fewer, targeted preloads, the critical content appears sooner.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: Adding preload to every resource always improves page speed.
misconceptions.correction: Preload raises a resource's priority; preloading many files makes them compete and can delay what's truly critical. Use preload only for critical resources discovered late, and measure the effect.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In "The preload pile-up", why did the page get slower?

analogy.example: Loading resources is like **preparing a stage show**: the set (stylesheet) must be up before the curtain opens; some actors (defer/module scripts) can arrive while the audience sits down. Rushing every prop to the front door at once (preload everything) jams the entrance.
usefulFor: remembering what must be ready first
seeing preload as a priority pass, not a speed boost
limitations: Shows start once; pages may keep loading resources.
Browsers schedule downloads automatically — hints only adjust priority.

nearTransfer.prompt: A page has three scripts: a chat widget (not critical), the main app (needs the DOM), and a tiny inline theme setter that must run before paint. Choose loading attributes for each.
expectedEvidence: Chat: async or defer; app: defer or module.
Theme setter: small inline script in head.

farTransfer.prompt: Record a Performance profile of one of your pages. Identify render-blocking and parser-blocking resources, change attributes, and compare the before/after timings.
scaffold: Change one thing at a time.

remediation.explanation: For each resource ask: **Is it needed before the first paint?** Yes → normal stylesheet / tiny inline script. No → defer, module or async. Preload only if critical and discovered late.

recap.summary: To configure document resources, link the main stylesheet normally (it's a render dependency), load scripts with defer or type="module" so parsing isn't blocked, and use preload only for a few critical late-discovered files — then measure the loading relationship in DevTools.
